name: tutorial-trigger-input
title: Trigger Input
description: Demonstrates the unified Trigger Input contract (ADR-0012) across every field type it supports: string, number, boolean, date, datetime, select, multiselect, textarea and object. triggerInput is the workflow's total input contract and every trigger validates against it, so ${triggerPayload.<field>} reads identically no matter which one fired. Start it by hand (the Start Run form renders one widget per type, including a JSON textarea for `object`), POST {"source":"edc","priority":"urgent","domains":["AE"],"sourceRecord":{"subjectId":"S-014"}} to its webhook, or attach a cron row carrying that same object as its static payload — all three produce the same triggerPayload, and a field the firing omits falls back to its declared `default` on every path. Triggers themselves are independent table resources managed via `mediforce workflow trigger-*` (ADR-0011, Issue #932).

triggerInput.name: source
triggerInput.description: Data source identifier. The only required field: a firing that omits it is rejected on every path, because no `default` covers it.

triggerInput.name: batchSize
triggerInput.description: Records per batch. A number, not a numeric string — a webhook posting "100" is rejected. Omitted firings (a cron row, a body without the key) land on 100.

triggerInput.name: dryRun
triggerInput.description: Process without persisting. A supplied `false` is a value, not an omission, so it is never replaced by the default.

triggerInput.name: priority
triggerInput.description: One of `options` — anything else is rejected. Drives the routing below via `variables.record.priority`.

triggerInput.name: domains
triggerInput.description: SDTM domains to process. An array whose every item must be in `options`; a `required` multiselect additionally rejects an empty array.

triggerInput.name: cutoffDate
triggerInput.description: Data cutoff, a date string any `Date.parse` accepts (`2026-03-31`). Optional and defaultless, so an omitting firing simply has no `cutoffDate` key.

triggerInput.name: startsAt
triggerInput.description: Instant to process from, validated like `date` but carrying a time (`2026-03-31T09:15:00.000Z`). The Start Run form submits it as a UTC ISO string.

triggerInput.name: notes
triggerInput.description: Free text for the run log. Same string validation as `string` — only the manual form's widget differs.

triggerInput.name: sourceRecord
triggerInput.description: The escape hatch for input this workflow does not enumerate — a proxied third-party body nests under this one key. Must be a JSON object: an array or a scalar is rejected, so `${triggerPayload.sourceRecord.<key>}` always has something to walk. There is deliberately no `array` type.

steps.name: Record the firing
steps.description: Reads the validated input the same way for every trigger kind. `triggerPayload.*` is the contract — a single `${...}` placeholder returns the value with its type intact, so `batchSize` stays a number and `sourceRecord` stays an object. `triggerContext.*` is the transport escape hatch, empty on a manual start, so a step depending on it has knowingly coupled itself to one trigger kind.

steps.name: Process Data
steps.description: A script step reads the trigger payload from /output/input.json, where the run's triggerPayload fields sit at the top level and previous step outputs are under `steps.<id>`.
